text:
maria: heads up — starting ~09:10 UTC we saw a bunch of model-serving gRPC streams hang on gpu-pool-us-east. tail latencies go to 30–60s and then the stream resumes. No pod restarts on the app side. Anyone touching networking?

devin: saw that too, reproducing on a canary. tcp retransmits and a lot of IP fragments in tcpdump. grabbing pcap now.

maria: ok can you paste the tcpdump snippet?

devin: here's the relevant tail (filtered for src/dst between pods):
```
12:34:10.123456 IP 10.10.5.23.50052 > 10.10.7.11.52000: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12489, ack 9876, win 64240, length 1444
12:34:10.123789 IP (DF) 10.10.5.23 > 10.10.7.11: frag 0:1400@0\/0
12:34:10.124012 IP 10.10.5.23 > 10.10.7.11: frag 1400:288@1400\/0
12:34:10.130000 IP 10.10.7.11 > 10.10.5.23: Flags [R], seq 9877, win 0, length 0
```
devin: looks like big payloads are being fragmented across the overlay and some fragments drop, gRPC stalls while retransmitting.

liam: which CNI + encap are those nodes running? vxlan/geneve?

raj: gpu-pool nodes are on Calico with VXLAN encapsulation, default calico mtu=1440 set in daemonset. Host NICs are set to 9000 (jumbo) via cloud-init for GPU RDMA tests last month.

maria: so host MTU 9000 + overlay MTU 1440 -> packets get encapsulated and exceed underlying path MTU, causing fragmentation. any recent kernel updates that might affect GSO/GRO?

devin: we rolled a kernel patch on those nodes 3 days ago (centos-gpu-kernel-6.1.9). I see GSO offload flags toggled to "off" on some hosts: run `ethtool -k eth0 | grep gso` shows gso: off. That will force software fragmentation on large frames.

raj: ok plausible chain: host NIC jumbos + overlay small MTU + GSO off -> libnet splits things into fragments and some fragments drop through vxlan path -> gRPC stream blocks waiting for lost fragment retransmit.

liam: confirmed from `ip link` on a node:
```
2: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
3: caliXXXXX: mtu 1440 qdisc noqueue state UP
```
liam: and calico daemonset has env CALICO_IPV4POOL_IPIP=Always? actually it's vxlan.

maria: impact: some in-flight GPU inference streams stall and cause client-side retries. This increases job wall time and billing while pods wait and eventually succeed. Need a short mitigation and a long-term fix.

devin: quick mitigation options:
- set net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 to help with path MTU discovery (non-invasive)
- re-enable GSO/GRO on hosts if kernel change flipped it (fast)
- set calico host mtu to 9000 (requires calico restart across nodes)
- change calico encap to no-encap for the GPU pool (needs host network changes)

raj: for immediate impact I can toggle tcp_mtu_probing=1 and try re-enabling GSO on one canary host. We should NOT change calico mtu cluster-wide without a plan.

maria: please canary the host-level fixes on one worker in gpu-pool-us-east then measure gRPC stream success for 30m. @raj take lead and post back.

raj: starting canary now on ip-10-10-5-23. commands: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` and `ethtool -K eth0 gso on gro on tso on`.

raj: after toggling, canary shows no fragment logs and stream latency normalized. tcpdump snippet now:
```
12:47:30.567890 IP 10.10.5.23.50052 > 10.10.7.11.52000: Flags [P.], seq 1:2000, ack 1, win 64240, length 1999
12:47:30.568012 IP 10.10.7.11 > 10.10.5.23: Flags [.], ack 2000, win 64240, length 0
```
raj: gRPC stream runs smooth.

maria: great. next steps? we should pick a long-term path — either unify MTU (set calico mtu to 9000) or set calico to use no-encap for gpu-pool or change host NICs back to 1500. Each has tradeoffs.

liam: setting calico mtu to 9000 might be safest since most clusters already have jumbo enabled for storage and RDMA tests. But updating calico DS requires rolling restarts of calico/node — must be staged.

devin: alternative: make calico use host-mtu detection (there's a Calico setting to `ipPools[].ipipMode` or `vxlanMode` and `mtu` templating per node). We can patch daemonset to set `FELIX_INTNETMTU=9000` on GPU nodes via nodeSelector.

raj: operational plan proposal:
1) Patch calico daemonset to add a nodeSelector for gpu-pool and set FELIX_INTNETMTU=9000 in a new calico-node instance (canary on one node).
2) Monitor pod-to-pod throughput & tcpdump for 1h.
3) Roll to remaining gpu nodes if green.
4) Re-enable GSO cluster-wide if any nodes have it disabled.

maria: add rollback: if any pod fails to establish overlay routes, revert the daemonset change immediately. Also create a k8s Pod disruption budget for calico patch.

devin: I'll prepare the calico DS YAML for the canary and a kubeapply plan with exact commands.

k8s-deploy-bot: deploy request queued: canary/calico-gpu-mtu-update -> env FELIX_INTNETMTU=9000 -> target nodes label gpu=true. CI checks passed.

raj: starting canary deploy in 2m. will post telemetry after 30m.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-452 (mtu-induced gRPC stalls on gpu-pool-us-east). Owner: raj. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-452 :thumbsup:

maria: thanks team. after we stabilize, let's add a test to our node rollout checklist to ensure offloads and MTU consistency are validated before kernel rollouts.

raj: noted. adding to runbook and change window checklist.

maria: nice catch. :clap:
